expectations.text: Output contains at least one specific numeric token count estimate for a file or total
expectations.evidence: The output contains numerous specific numeric token count estimates. Examples include: global CLAUDE.md ~1,972 tokens, parent CLAUDE.md ~8,107 tokens, project CLAUDE.md ~9,062 tokens, total startup ~19,141 tokens, docs/IDEAL_MASTER_PLAN.md 30,520 tokens, grand total 275,692 tokens, and many more per-file estimates throughout the tables.

expectations.text: Output provides a breakdown of token usage by file or section (not just a single total)
expectations.evidence: The output provides extensive per-file breakdown across multiple tables: (1) Session startup breakdown: 3 CLAUDE.md files with individual token counts (1,972 / 8,107 / 9,062); (2) Root-level files table: 5 files with individual token counts; (3) docs/ section table: 34 files each with individual token counts; (4) Summary table by category (Root MD files 56,496 / docs/ 219,196). The breakdown is thorough and multi-level.

claims: Session startup costs ~19,141 tokens across 3 CLAUDE.md files
Project CLAUDE.md alone is 9,062 tokens (3.6x over ~2,500 token target)
Parent CLAUDE.md is 8,107 tokens with significant duplication
docs/ folder contains 34 files totaling ~219,196 tokens
Grand total of 275,692 tokens across 39 documentation files
Potential savings of ~12,169 tokens (~60-63%) with optimization
No .claudeignore file exists in the project

suggestions: Output is thorough and well-structured with consistent per-file token breakdowns
Both a tiered structure (session startup vs full repo) and per-file granularity are present
Methodology is explicitly stated (ASCII/4 + Cyrillic/2 formula), which adds credibility
Optimization recommendations are backed by specific numbers, not just vague advice
eval_feedback.overall: Both expectations are fully met. The output excels at providing specific numeric token estimates at every level — individual files, sections (session startup / root files / docs/), and grand totals. The breakdown is multi-dimensional: by file, by category, and by loading tier (essential / on-demand / archive). This is a high-quality token analysis output.
